statement: In Hawaii, an adult name change is granted by the Office of the Lieutenant Governor rather than by a court. Only current Hawaii residents are eligible for a name change granted this way.
detail: You pay a $50.00 filing fee, a $1.00 archive fee, and a $5.00 service fee — all non-refundable — plus a separate newspaper publication fee (starting around $204.19) and a $41 registration fee to record your order at the Bureau of Conveyances. The process to change your name may take 8 to 12 weeks. A name change isn't necessary if you're a Hawaii resident who was married in Hawaii and declared your spouse's name on your marriage certificate, or if you're divorced and your divorce decree stipulates resuming a maiden name or previous name.

cost.note: Several separate fees apply: $50 filing, $1 archive, and $5 service (paid to the Lieutenant Governor's office), plus a newspaper publication fee starting around $204.19 and a $41 Bureau of Conveyances registration fee. No single combined total is published.

source.title: State of Hawaii — Online Name Change Application (Office of the Lieutenant Governor)

topic: Hawaii driver's license or state ID name change
statement: To change your name on a Hawaii driver's license or state ID card, make an AlohaQ appointment at a Driver Licensing Center, complete the Driver's License Application Form, and submit proof of your name change.
detail: At your appointment you'll also take a vision test and be fingerprinted, then pay the required fee and have your photo taken. The county's page links to a separate downloadable document listing which proof-of-name-change documents it accepts; read that document before your appointment to confirm what to bring.

cost.note: This page does not state the fee amount for a name-change transaction.

source.title: City and County of Honolulu, Department of Customer Services — Driver's License Procedures

topic: Hawaii driver's license or state ID gender designation
statement: Hawaii's driver's license and state ID application forms let you select your own gender designation — Male, Female, or Not Specified — as one of the boxes you check on the application. The form does not ask for any supporting document to back up that choice.
detail: This same three-option field appears on both the State of Hawaii Driver's License Application and the State of Hawaii Identification Card Application. Bring your completed application to an appointment at a Driver Licensing Center to submit it.

source.title: State of Hawaii Driver's License Application

statement: Hawaii's Department of Health does not describe a general process for updating the name on a birth certificate just because you obtained a court-ordered legal name change. Its published list of birth-certificate amendments covers five specific situations: adoption, a new birth certificate for a sex-designation change, a legal determination that a listed parent is not the parent, a correction to surname or paternity information made under law, and a foreign adoption finalized in Hawaii.
detail: If your situation is not one of these five, contact the Department of Health's Corrections Section directly at (808) 586-4541 to ask whether an amendment is possible — this page does not say either way. Do not assume a Hawaii birth certificate will show a new name after an ordinary court name change.

source.title: Hawaii Department of Health — Amended Certificate of Birth

statement: To get a new Hawaii birth certificate with a different sex designation, Hawaii law (HRS section 338-17.7) requires a notarized affidavit from a U.S.-licensed physician stating that the physician has an established relationship with you, has evaluated your medical history, and confirms that you have completed appropriate clinical treatment for gender transition.
detail: You complete an Application for Amendment to Birth Record and a Physician Affidavit Form for Sex Designation Change; a doctor of naturopathy cannot serve as the certifying physician under Hawaii law. The fee is $3 for each amended item on the certificate. The new certificate substitutes for the original, which is sealed and can only be reopened by a court order or at the birth registrant's own request. If you also want your current legal name reflected, you must have already completed a legal name change before applying.

cost.note: A fee of $3 is charged for each amendment of an item on the certificate.

source.title: Hawaii Department of Health — New Birth Certificate for Sex Designation Change
